summary:
Item 'private', finished after the review (verdict accept_after_fixes). Both must_fix findings are fixed and tested, and so are the cheap should_fix points. The reviewed patch applied cleanly to a fresh worktree at e4ce22b. The rewritten patch has 21 files, 658 lines added and 241 removed. It applies to a clean HEAD (git apply --check on a git archive of HEAD). Nothing was committed.
MUST_FIX 1, the run_case glue untested: new class test_rail_demo_campaign.TheSceneCaseWhereItsNamesAreFound. It calls cases_scene.run_case in this process, the way a child of the runner calls it, on Rail Demo built by fixture.rail_demo_workspace in an attempt environment. The scene it plays is P01 said in invented names ('Night bench readings', 'Peak duration' and so on), with an entry for rail_demo that finds each name there by the words of the After Hours 07 entry. It checks four things: the case scores Pass on the scene's own checks; it notes which names were found; the window read Rail Demo's names; and every observation is said back in the scene's names. With said_back removed, 2 of its 3 tests fail (outcome Partial). With find_names replaced by {}, 2 of 3 fail.
MUST_FIX 2, find_names: a sheet is now counted by record, so two sheets of one title are refused in words ('2 sheets say "rev b current" (for Rail Demo limits Rev B CURRENT)') instead of a bare KeyError or a silent pass. A sheet's id is taken only after that check. Calculations and rows are still found by name; the docstring says so. Two new stand-in desks are in test_each_name_is_found_once. On the reviewed code that test fails: 'ValueError not raised : 2 sheets say "bench readings"'.
SHOULD_FIX done: (1) A01: the 'pdf_source_sha' observation is dropped. A new test runs DA01's own function on Rail Demo through a kernel that gives the sheet's own source hash otherwise: the check reads False, and with the real kernel it reads True. The reviewer's mutation M3 (found() taking the sheet's own hash) now fails that test. (2) cases_anchor.found pages intake.items 100 at a time. (3) found() passes over a calculation it cannot read and names it if a calculation lookup then finds nothing. (4) found()'s reads are logged as the case's own op lines (records passes ctx.progress). field.read and intake.items are added to the allowed lists of A01, A16 and A27 and their twins. Tests check that every read in DA01 and DA27 is allowed. (5) A27 keeps the three ids it needs (sheet, settled calculation, settled finding; no hash) in its checkpoint, and the resumed phase works on them without finding again. (6) docs/CAMPAIGN.md and the fixture.py docstring now say the campaign keeps nothing of the backup, while the release notes of 0.4 to 0.8.2 still quote some of it and are left for the owner to decide.
On the owner's backup, two checks are weaker than before: A16 no longer checks the open sheet's title, and A27 no longer checks that the settled calculation keeps its name after the recheck. DA16 and DA27 still check both on Rail Demo.

decisions: find_names counts sheets by record, but calculations and rows by name. A sheet is pointed at by its title and its rows are read from it, so two records of one title cannot be told apart. For a calculation or a row the swap uses only the name, so two records of one name do no harm. Refusing them could stop the case on the backup for nothing (cases_anchor.found separately requires exactly one calculation per pair of inputs). The docstring says so.

The run_case test runs in-process, not through the runner, because the runner's children cannot see a patched scene. It builds Rail Demo with the runner's own fixture.rail_demo_workspace in fixture.attempt_environment, patches only cases_scene.load, and scores with core.score, as child_main does. It holds the seed with seed_hold.seed_bound, as test_rail_demo does, so it runs even on an edited seed.

found() takes an optional progress callback (records passes ctx.progress) instead of using ctx.call, so that found(kernel, owner) still works on its own in tests. It writes the same 'op' line that Attempt.call writes.
A calculation found() cannot read is passed over and named only when one of the two calculation lookups then finds nothing. It is not named for the finding or the PDF, where it plays no part.
Adding field.read and intake.items to the allowed lists changes the revisions of A01, A16, A27, DA01, DA16 and DA27. Results recorded before are of the older revision.

A27's checkpoint keeps only the three ids it uses, and no hash. The reviewer had pointed out that a hash in a local result file is the owner's. On the backup, the local checkpoint does hold the owner's record ids, as the local result files already did.
The phrase 'settled draw' in docs/MODEL_TRIAL_03.md (a model's own paraphrase, in a bracketed answer) was left as it is. It is generic wording, not a value or a title. The coordinator may bracket it.
No new test module, so tools/check_hatch.py FOCUSED_MODULES is unchanged. I disagreed with no finding.

release_note: Graphite's campaign code, its cases and the playable scene no longer carry anything from your own After Hours 07 workspace: no record ids, no file hash, no titles and none of your readings. The scene is now written on Rail Demo, the invented workspace kept in the program. When your backup is present, the scene and the four anchor cases find what they need in it as they run, by what each thing is, and refuse in words if something is missing or there twice. The numbers they expect there are the ones the first-run workshop already prints. The release notes of 0.4 to 0.8.2 still quote some of your titles and readings, and older commits still hold the earlier values; both are left for you to decide.
